events.title: Telegram
events.text:
The UAE is redesigning parts of its planned 5GW Abu Dhabi AI campus after Iranian drone and missile attacks exposed the vulnerability of Gulf data centers.
Officials are considering dedicated air defenses around the compute clusters and underground or hardened facilities for critical servers, power and cooling infrastructure.
The attacks damaged AWS facilities and other UAE infrastructure, while Iran’s IRGC later identified G42’s planned campus among potential targets.
Construction has not stopped. The first 200MW phase is reportedly nearing completion, with executives saying work “never stopped.” 
OpenAI’s planned 1GW Stargate UAE cluster remains part of the larger project.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
BREAKING: Yemen's Houthis seized Perim (Mayyun) Island and completed control of the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait. 
Reuters separately reports they've reached Dhubab, the coastal city directly on the strait. 
The Houthis now control nearly the entire Yemeni Red Sea coast.
This is arguably the most strategically significant territorial gain in the entire Yemen war. 
Perim sits in the middle of the 29 km-wide strait and physically splits it into two shipping channels. 
Holding the island plus the adjacent coastline means the Houthis can threaten passing ships with artillery and short-range weapons — not just longer-range missiles and drones from further inland.
The strategic nightmare is now real. 
Iran already controls pressure on Hormuz. 
Saudi Arabia has been routing more oil west through the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to bypass Hormuz. 
The Houthis have now closed off that workaround at the exit point. 
Both of the Middle East's critical shipping chokepoints are under Iranian-axis pressure simultaneously. 
There is no easy third route. Roughly 10% of global seaborne trade normally passes through Bab-el-Mandeb.
Brent crude is above $107. 
Source: AFP, Reuters

events.text:
US builds $1.2M 'bunker-buster lab' after failing to crack Iran’s underground sites
 
The Pentagon is spending millions trying to solve a problem it has already struggled with: how to destroy Iran’s deeply buried nuclear infrastructure.
 
👉 Several days before the conflict with Iran began in late February, the Pentagon’s Defense Threat Reduction Agency published a document showing it had awarded almost a $1.2 million contract to upgrade a “unique subterranean test facility” at White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico for a live-fire test aimed at developing capabilities against emerging underground threats.
 
Since early March, the remote location known as the Alternate Seismic Hardrock in Situ Test Site has continued to accumulate excavations, with the test site also carved into granite, similarly to Pickaxe Mountain.
 
➡️ Now, the US is reportedly preparing new tests at the simulated underground facility to develop methods for striking Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain site—a hardened underground complex near Natanz that Washington and Israel believe houses Iran’s enriched uranium stockpiles.
 
President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to target the site, arguing that hitting the underground facility would be necessary to limit Iran’s nuclear capabilities.
 
The challenge for the US is that even its largest conventional bunker-busting weapons may not guarantee the destruction of facilities built deep underground. Earlier strikes on facilities such as Natanz and Fordow were presented as major blows, yet Iran maintained the ability to preserve key underground infrastructure and continue operations.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🔥🇨🇳 China’s nuclear subs just got a missile built to reach the US
 
The Chinese navy is refitting its fleet of nuclear-powered submarines to carry the new JL-3 intercontinental ballistic missile, Taipei Times reports.
 
The JL-3 is expected to become a key pillar of China’s nuclear arsenal, strengthening the country’s ability to retaliate in the event of an enemy attack. 
 
Here’s why: 
 
🔴 The missile’s 10,000 km range allows China to target the northwestern US, as well as Alaska, Guam and Hawaii, from Chinese waters 
 
🔴 The JL-3 is capable of carrying multiple independently targetable re-entry vehicles, with at least three nuclear warheads per missile
 
🔴 An estimated yield of each warhead is around 250 to 1,000 kilotons, enabling a single missile to strike multiple targets
 
🔴 Unlike liquid-fuel missiles, the JL-3 uses solid fuel, making it easier to maintain aboard submarines while keeping it ready for launch
 
The JL-3 is therefore set to strengthen the sea-based leg of China's nuclear triad, giving the PLA a more survivable long-range strike capability from its submarine fleet.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

🔥 Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline on fire — another Houthi's win
Satellite imagery suggests Yemen's Houthis have directly hit Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pipeline in the desert southeast of Medina — a strike on the kingdom's most strategic energy artery.
🌏 Sentinel-3 imagery from today reveals a massive black smoke plume nearly 100 km long stretching across the desert between Medina and Mahd adh Dhahab
🌏 NASA FIRMS fire data shows multiple heat anomalies clustered along a stretch of under 10 km
🌏 Fire radiative power above 70 megawatts — more than double a conventional fire
🌏 The burn sustained for at least 8 hours
The East-West pipeline carries Saudi crude from Abqaiq to Yanbu on the Red Sea — the kingdom's only export route that does not pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The one corridor the kingdom built specifically to survive a Hormuz closure.
